text:
Maya: Heads up — merged Auric's LoRA into the staging branch and ran the quick eval pack. Seeing a small tokenization shift on a subset of customer prompts.
Jasper: Ugh, what kind of shift? percentages or just weird truncation?
Maya: Mostly token count delta. Example prompt that changed: 
`How do I reset my device?` used to be 7 tokens, now shows 8 in our tokenizer. Not massive but affects prefix caching.
Ravi: Can you paste tokenizer outputs?
Maya: Sure:
```
# before (base tokenizer)
[CLS] How do I reset my device ? [SEP]
Tokens: [101, 157, 24, 11, 403, 98, 102]
# after (with Auric LoRA applied via merge)
[CLS] How do I reset my device ? [SEP]
Tokens: [101, 157, 24, 11, 403, 57, 98, 102]
```
Elena: That extra split looks like a subword merge change. Might be from a tokenizer config mismatch during model export. Did we reserialize the tokenizer from their repo?
Maya: No, we used our standard HF-tokenizer->fast pipeline, and then applied the LoRA weights. Auric provided a small tokenizer.json but we didn't load it by default.
Jasper: That explains it. If the customer expects their tokenizer, outputs will differ. Two remediation paths: 1) load Auric tokenizer in the model packaging step, or 2) normalize prompts via our canonical tokenizer before caching.
Ravi: For quick mitigation, can we add a pre-tokenization check that compares token counts between base and merged variants and flags >1 token delta?
Maya: I ran a batch of 200 prompts from their smokepack. Stats: 
```
N=200
# token_count_delta distribution
delta=0 -> 172
delta=1 -> 23
delta=2 -> 4
delta=3 -> 1
```
Elena: Those 4-5 cases with delta>=2 are risky for KV-cache alignment. We should block the canary rollout until we resolve.
ops-bot: deploy-check failed: token-mismatch >=2 detected on canary (auric-lora-staging).
Jasper: Agreed — block canary. Maya, can you try repackaging with Auric's tokenizer.json and rerun the same smokepack? If that fixes >99% of cases, we can enable a tokenizer-preserve flag for customer-specific adapters.
Maya: Starting a repack job now. ETA ~12m. I'll post results.
qa-bot: Quick suggestion: add a lightweight indicator in the eval report: "tokenizer_source": ["redwood-default"|"customer-supplied"]. Makes triage faster.
Ravi: Good call. Also log the exact token diffs for the top 10 failing prompts so we can show Auric evidence.
Maya: Repacks done. Results with Auric tokenizer loaded: 
```
N=200
delta=0 -> 197
delta=1 -> 2
delta=2 -> 1
```
Maya: Can confirm major reduction. The one delta=2 looks like a punctuation edge-case, will inspect.
Elena: Cool. Next steps: 1) add tokenizer-preserve flag to packaging API (opt-in per customer) 2) add token-delta check in pre-canary gates 3) update rollout docs.
Jasper: I'll raise a RFC for the packaging change and include a migration note for Dedicated/Private customers.
Maya: Filing follow-ups: PR for pre-canary check (link soon), packaging RFC, and I'll attach the failing prompt examples.
Ravi: If we enable tokenizer-preserve, add a note about model signature/hash so the routing layer can match cached prefixes only to identical tokenizer+model combos.
Elena: Yep — prefix cache key should include tokenizer-hash.
Maya: Thanks all. Reopening canary once pre-canary checks pass. :thumbsup:
